THE TASK

Follow a commanded forward, lateral and yaw velocity on flat ground, stairs and moderate rough terrain. A gait clock shapes the reward. The network chooses joint targets; a PD controller produces torque. Route selection comes from the operator: this stack supplies locomotion.

Signal / sourceDimTeacherStudentCriticProcessing / meaning

PERCEPTION, STEP BY STEP

1,440 rays become 99 terrain values.

  1. Cast from the head. 90 azimuth directions × 16 vertical rings; 360° / 4°, elevations −80° to −10°, range 5 m. Approximate mount [0.28, 0, 0.03] m; rays rotate with the body.
  2. Filter and bin points. Keep z ∈ [−0.90, +0.45] m relative to the base, reject the trunk box, and fill the yaw-aligned 1.0 × 0.8 m grid at 0.1 m spacing.
  3. Estimate the surface. Use the lower 20% quantile with at least 2 returns per cell and a 0.075 m cell radius. Reject maps below 50% coverage.
  4. Encode relative height. clip(base_z − ground_z − 0.25, −1, 1). Higher ground is negative. Missing cells are zero, which also represents nominal flat ground.
  5. Learn under corruption. Point jitter, map drift, outliers, missing cells, blind episodes and 0–60 ms map delay teach robust fusion.

The teacher’s 99 heights come from a separate ideal vertical ray grid, with origins 0.5 m above the base. The student receives the map built from LiDAR. Camera images and raw point clouds are not network inputs.

Exact noise, latency and sensor limitations
03 / NETWORK ANATOMY

Open the black box.

Read left to right. Select any module for its layers, formula, role in training and source. B is the number of parallel robots; all dimensions are per robot.

Hidden MLP layers use ELU. Output layers are linear unless a sigmoid gate is shown. Empirical normalization maintains running statistics for body / privileged inputs; bounded terrain heights bypass it.

Three different uses of memory. The teacher receives explicit 84-value history. The student has a 256-unit GRU. The external 32-value terrain gate learns how much to trust current perception; it is separate from the GRU’s internal reset and update gates.

04 / LEARNING ALGORITHMS

Two objectives.
One behaviour.

The teacher discovers locomotion through rewards. The student receives action labels and reconstruction targets at the states it actually visits.

?

What happens when an episode ends?

A timeout or fall triggers a reset for the affected environment. The runner clears that robot’s recurrent memory; other robots keep theirs. At the truncation boundary, the student detaches the computation graph while carrying forward memory values. On deployment, entering the policy state resets the ONNX hidden state.

Generic modules versus the active PGTT path

The repository also contains standard PPO ActorCritic policies, generic recurrent policies, generic Distillation, RND, symmetry augmentation and tracking tasks. The PGTT registrations use ActorCriticWild → PPO and StudentTeacherWild → DistillationWild. Generic distillation.py supplies shared infrastructure; the specialized class adds belief reconstruction. RND and symmetry are not enabled in this PGTT recipe.

05 / THE TRAINING WORLD

The ground is part
of the algorithm.

Terrain changes what the robot sees, which states it visits and which actions receive reward. The task recipe connects all three.

SCHEMATIC · CONFIGURATION RANGES, NOT A PHYSICS SIMULATION
GAIT / TERRAIN-AWARE REWARD

A clock encourages a trot.

Episode frequency ∈ [1, 3] Hz. Diagonal phase offsets are [0, π, π, 0] in FL, FR, RL, RR order. The observation contains 4 cosines, 4 sines and frequency.

The foot-phase reward compares measured foot height above the terrain to a smooth swing target: stance ≈ 0.022 m; swing apex = 0.08 + clamp(local terrain range, 0, 0.15) m. Nearby terrain is sampled within 0.15 m. This reward encourages clearance; the policy still produces joint targets.

CURRICULUM / RESET / TIMING

Harder terrain, gradually.

10 difficulty rows × 20 columns of 8 × 8 m patches; 20 m border. Moving more than 4 m advances difficulty. Moving less than half of the commanded episode distance lowers it. Uniform rough height noise does not scale with difficulty.

Penalty weights ramp from 10% to full strength over 1,500 × 24 environment steps. Episodes last up to 20 s. Training terminates when tilt exceeds 90°. The real controller has a tighter 1 rad tilt guard.

Physics uses a 0.005 s timestep, with four substeps per policy decision. Commands are sampled every 8–12 s with x, y and yaw-rate bounds [−1, 1]; 5% are standing commands.

REWARD BALANCE

What PPO is being asked to do.

r = Δt Σ wᵢ rᵢ · Δt = 0.02 s
Domain randomization and exact event configuration

Base mass / COM, link mass, friction, PD gains, torque limits, encoder bias, actuator delay, pushes and external wrenches vary during training. Nominal evaluation removes noise and disturbances; stress evaluation retains them.

A REPEATABLE RESEARCH LOOP
  1. State the hypothesisChange one factor; preserve a baseline and configuration snapshot.
  2. Inspect, then smoke testCheck dimensions, noise, rewards and NaNs before a long run.
  3. Train matched policiesKeep teacher / student architecture and observation contracts compatible.
  4. Evaluate a matrixFlat · stairs · rough × seeds 42 / 43 / 44 × nominal / randomized × LiDAR / blind.
  5. Inspect failuresCompare tracking, falls, distance, episode length, losses and terrain coverage.
  6. Export and check parityRetain the checkpoint, command, configuration and export manifest.

Matching joints, maps and clocks

Export writes policy.onnx, deploy.yaml and export_manifest.json. Joint order, normalizers, gains, action scale and map parameters come from the saved configuration. The SDK reorder is [3, 4, 5, 0, 1, 2, 9, 10, 11, 6, 7, 8].

The C++ controller runs the policy at 50 Hz inside a 1 kHz FSM. PD gains: Kp = 20, Kd = 1; actuator effort limit 23.5 N·m. A 100 ms policy watchdog and 1 rad tilt guard protect the control loop.

A real height map needs a bridge

ROS 2 PointCloud2 + TF / odometry → rolling 0.4 s cloud in a gravity-aligned world frame → latest base pose → identical grid → 99 little-endian float32 values on UDP 9870, at up to 20 Hz.

Cloud / pose freshness limits are 0.15 s. Coverage must reach 50%. Controller map timeout is 0.2 s, then it supplies zeros. Zero is the trained missing-map representation; it does not guarantee blind stair capability. Match the physical LiDAR transform, timing, frames and driver.

RESEARCH & HARDWARE STATUS

Locomotion still has to be proven.

The checked checkpoints are smoke runs, not a fully trained deployment policy. Full terrain evaluations, physical LiDAR calibration, aarch64 runtime checks and controlled real-robot trials remain necessary. This atlas documents the implementation, not a claim of hardware readiness.
